exclusionsInForce.name: MenorahStoneOfThreeSteps
exclusionsInForce.why: The menorah's stone of three steps inside the Heikhal, on which the kohen stands to dress the lamps (Rambam, Hilkhot Beit HaBechirah 3:11). Two reasons to leave it on the existing Trim. (1) Idiom: drafted-margin work is the dressing of a monumental retaining wall - it is what the Temple Mount's outer faces were given, not what a small dressed furnishing inside the sanctuary was given. No source I found treats the menorah's step-stone as ashlar work, and Shmuel's instruction is about 'the temple stones used for wall'. (2) Scale: the Trim drafted margin is 5.6-10.7 cm wide, so on a tread of roughly 50-60 cm the margin would cover most of the surface and the boss would be a sliver. Recorded per slot in every plan and apply receipt under excludedSlots.
